evidence.quoted_text:
"manager_restarted": (
            (((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
             .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                 .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            and bool(((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and bool(((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")),
evidence.reason: The current `manager_restarted` predicate accepts differing nonempty PIDs and invocation IDs without checking that both manager snapshots came from the same boot. A guest reboot between the before/after manager inspections can therefore satisfy `manager_restarted`, falsely proving an isolated manager restart; the adjacent `boot_id_changed` logic covers only the reboot snapshots. Adding nonempty, equal boot IDs to the manager snapshot pair is a routine correctness fix and preserves the existing PID/invocation checks.
